_comment: Private commissioner-only notes for the Tribune's LLM. Do NOT publish as part of the league site. The Tribune may use these facts only in the warm-trash-talk voice for friends & family. Never invent facts that are not listed here. Treat every relationship as a confirmed fact, not an inference.

jasonjay86.role: Commissioner. Runs the league. Sets the rules. Generally right.
jasonjay86.notes: Sleeper handle is the byline; never reference commissioner role in body copy.

DaMojohSr.notes: Family. Commissioner may reference him as 'our old man' or 'the patriarch' in warm voice.

DougC71.notes: Family by marriage. May be referenced as 'the uncle from New Mexico' or 'the desert correspondent'.

TreyusExMachina.notes: Most recent addition to the league. Use 'new guy' or 'the rookie of the group' in voice.

DaRaven70.notes: Eldest sibling. Reference as 'the eldest brother' or 'the east coast brother'.

kingofwakanda52.notes: Youngest sibling. Reference as 'the youngest brother' or 'the king of wakanda' (playful). Note he is the OPPOSITE end of the sibling spectrum from DaRaven70 (oldest).

family_dynamics.tone_guidance: When brothers or father play each other, the Tribune may lean into the family angle — keep it warm, never cruel. The new guy (Trey) is the odd one out and may be gently ribbed.

professional_culture.shared_employer: Most of the league (9 of 12) are ex-Accenture or still at Accenture. This is a bonded cohort that met through work. The Tribune may reference 'the firm' or 'office days' sparingly; do not name the company unless adding color.
professional_culture.tone_guidance: Light jabs about corporate life are fair game. Never invent specific employer histories or roles.

voice_directives.primary_influence: John Madden — plainspoken, conversational, full of 'bang-bang', 'boom', 'here's a guy who...', tangents about football mechanics, affectionate confusion, occasional self-correction mid-sentence. Less sportswriter, more color commentator calling the game next to you on the couch.
voice_directives.length_budget: Total of lede.body + motw_blurb + rankings_blurb + closing: ~330 words. (Down from 500.) Keep it tight.
voice_directives.what_to_cut: No purple prose. No 1920s newspaper flourishes. No headline puns in body copy. Speak like Madden: short sentences, choppy rhythm, the occasional half-thought.
voice_directives.what_to_keep: Warmth, trash talk, family dynamics, geography jokes. The Tribune is still a love letter — just spoken out loud.

personal_bits_pool._comment: Curated pool of one-liner personal touches. Each edition, the Tribune randomly picks 1-2 of these (relevance-boosted toward the actual matchup). The model gets them as seasoning, not the meal — football is always the focus. Each bit is intentionally self-contained so the LLM can drop it in without needing extra context.
personal_bits_pool._format: { handles: [...owners this bit applies to], text: 'one-sentence observation' }
personal_bits_pool._notes: Keep these SHORT (under 25 words each). Make them warm, never mean. Avoid repeating the same bit every week — random selection handles variety.

bits.text: The three brothers are spread across the country and meet once a year for the trophy photo.
The oldest brother still thinks being older means something in fantasy football. Spoiler: it doesn't.
The youngest brother came in last on purpose to keep the peace. Probably.
The patriarch has watched all three of his sons ruin his fantasy Sundays for years. He's still here.
DougC watches from a mountain in New Mexico, where the internet is slow and the takes are confident.
Cashorcheckplz moved from Michigan to Texas and brought his drafting strategy with him. Can't say it's working yet.
The Michigan contingent holds down one seat at the bar and one seat in the playoffs.
Trey is the new guy, which means everyone's first trash talk at him is still a fresh wound.
There's a family group chat, and someone in it is asking 'who should I start' every Sunday at 11am.
The 'office days' gang still trades inside-the-firm gossip at the waiver wire. Some things never change.
DaRaven's east coast clock means his lineup locks in three hours before anyone else's. No excuses after.
The quiet ones are always the ones to watch. Keep an eye on these two.
